metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is predominantly negative (≥ 15 consecutive -1.00), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In high-sentiment volatility (alternating ±1.00), model overfits short-term noise; smooth 30d forecast with 5-day moving average to reduce erratic peaks.
- If true outcome is > 10% below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for next 5 days.
